language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The Q3 release is the first scheduled update of the cash runway since the Nov 18 royalty sale. BioLineRx sells its 14.4% APHEXDA royalty to Soleus for $5.6M, about 6x the roughly $0.9M a year that royalty yields at Q2's $1.6M a quarter of sales. Part of the money goes to a partial repayment of the BlackRock loan, which removes a $4M minimum-cash covenant. The Nov 18 release stated no new runway. The standing guide is 'into 1H 2027', set on $13.1M of cash at June 30. My estimate is about $11-12M at Sept 30 (13.1 + 3.3 net August raise - ~$3.5M quarterly burn - ~$1.1M loan amortisation), against a market cap of about $7M. A runway extended to 2H 2027 or beyond, plus net cash near the market cap, is the likely new content.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior prints, closes from Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BLRX?range=1y&interval=1d): Q3'25 on 2025-11-24 +7.7%; FY25 on 2026-03-23 -12.5%; Q1'26 on 2026-05-27 +6.6% (first GLIX1 patient); Q2'26 on 2026-08-31 +7.7%, the day after an offering-led drop. Runway was 'maintained' at each print, never extended. The royalty-sale day itself (2026-11-18) closed +2.7% on 295K volume, then gave it back (-8% over 2 sessions).

findings.finding: A steady, news-free decline into the print: closes went from $2.04 (Oct 23) to $0.99 (Nov 20), down on almost every session, with volume rising from 2-5K to 10-33K ADS a day. The only company news in the period was positive or neutral (SNO posters with no significant adverse events, 4th GLIX1 cohort dosing, the royalty sale). The likely seller is the August offering investor. Armistice holds ADSs from the $2.78 offering and had an F-1 resale registration filed 2026-09-25, and $2.78 warrants that are deep out of the money. Tax-loss selling in a name -74% from its high fits too. If that seller is not finished, it sells into whatever the print says.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August raise drew -5.8% on announcement (2.76 to 2.60) and a 20% drop reported in late August coverage. The royalty-sale day saw a +2.7% close quickly sold back down.

findings.finding: The motixafortide PDAC trial (CheMo4METPANC, NCT04543071) changed to 'Active, not recruiting' in its 2026-09-16 registry update, against the 'enrolling' wording in the company's Q2 release. The company has guided the prespecified interim/futility analysis (at 40% of PFS events) to happen 'in 2026'. So the Q3 release has to either report on it, reaffirm the 2026 timing or slip it to 2027. The market cap of about $7M is near net cash and puts almost no value on PDAC (Zacks models a 20% probability). A disclosed pass would be a large positive; a slip or futility would be a small negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No PDAC readout since the ASCO 2025 pilot data (4 of 11 progression-free for more than a year); its reaction is not in my sources. The 2026 guide was reaffirmed in March and August without a measurable move attributable to it.

findings.finding: The release will restate the UK sanctions position. Regulations enacted 2026-05-20 bar UK persons from facilitating maritime transport of Russian-origin LNG from 2027-01-01 for the long-term Yamal Trade charters of the Yenisei River and Lena River (to 2033 and 2034; 34.5% of H1 2026 revenue). The company must replace UK-based providers, including insurers, and said on Nov 3 there is 'no assurance that replacement services will be available on comparable terms, or at all'. Losing the charters 'could cause a default under the debt agreements'. The results come six weeks before the deadline: any progress on replacement insurers would be new and positive; a repeat of the Nov 3 wording, or a charterer dispute, would be negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 3 sanctions update (released 16:05 ET) was followed by 3.17 to 3.04 over the next two sessions, about -4%. No earlier print carried a deadline this close.

findings.finding: The two other sanctions regimes eased after the Q2 print. On 2026-10-16 an Executive Order waived nearly all of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act's Russia provisions, including those that would have reached Novatek as Yamal LNG's controlling shareholder (Act signed 2026-09-18). The EU's 21st package (adopted 2026-07-23) exempts legacy pre-2022 long-term contracts to at least 2027-07-25, and the company believes the Yamal charters qualify. The UK rule is the remaining live constraint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The US waiver week (Oct 16) saw the stock fall from 3.42 to 3.30, so the market did not reward the easing. No print reaction on this line.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-12, after the quarter, the partnership redeemed 2,000,000 of its 3,000,000 9.00% Series A preferred units at $25, a $50M cash outlay, from 'available liquidity'. Cash was $59.5M at 2026-06-30. The release will show the Sept 30 cash and, as a subsequent event, a much thinner balance going into the Jan 1 UK deadline. That deadline is one the company itself links to possible debt default. What the money buys: retiring 9% paper saves about $4.5M a year of preferred distributions, roughly $0.12 a common unit a year, which is accretive. What it costs is a liquidity cushion ahead of a sanctions cliff.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement day (2026-10-09) closed 3.70 to 3.60, -2.7%, and the slide continued afterwards. No print history on this line.

outside_window.finding: The $10M common unit repurchase program expires 2026-11-24. Last year's renewal was announced 2025-12-10, after the prior program expired 2025-11-21, so a renewal most likely lands after the exit window.
UK maritime services ban on Russian LNG takes effect for the Yamal charters on 2027-01-01. Whether the charters survive (insurer replacement, charterer stance) resolves then.

findings.finding: The brand owner is still funding the company and deepening its involvement. THRI (RBI) agreed in June to buy up to US$55m of additional senior secured convertible notes in four tranches through early 2027, each subject to business-performance milestone conditions; the first US$15.8m closed in July 2026. On 2026-10-19 RBI swapped its international president on the board for Stanford Ming Lin, Tim Hortons APAC GM since June 2026 and a former Cotti board member, to 'coordinate between brand owner and the China business'. The money buys marketing, product innovation and openings split evenly between company and franchise stores, as the CFO said and as the September marketing ramp confirms. Liquidity is tight (cash RMB121m, current liabilities RMB1,059m against current assets RMB295m), so whether a second tranche closed is the funding question the release answers.

outside_window.finding: At $1.00 the stock is at the Nasdaq $1.00 minimum bid threshold. If it stays below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days, a deficiency notice follows, and the company did a reverse split in January 2025 for the same reason. Any notice or split comes weeks after this window.

The second to fourth tranches of the US$55m THRI notes run to early 2027 and are subject to business-performance milestones. Closings after the window could make the release's disclosure moot or reverse it.

findings.finding: Q3 KPIs, pre-released 2026-10-15: GBV $437m (+30% YoY) against a company guide of $390-397m, ~11% above the top of the range; transactions 494k (+15%) against 481-490k. Platform revenue (Q2 $2.9m, +19%; Q3 2025 $2.6m) therefore likely prints ~$3.0-3.1m, at or above what the $7.7-7.8m revenue guide embedded. The release adds that 'GBV also reflected elevated freight rates', so part of the GBV beat is price, not take.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same setup twice. Q2 2026: KPI beat pre-released, revenue $7.7m beat the $7.2-7.4m guide, shares +14% pre-market (https://finviz.com/news/382895/freightos-shares-surge-14-as-q2-loss-beats-expectations). Q3 2025: KPI beat pre-released, revenue lagged estimates, stock -13.9% on the day (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CRGO/freightos-reports-third-quarter-2025-y3crjr4vg07w.html). The KPI beat alone has not decided the sign.

findings.finding: Solutions (software/data, ~62% of revenue: $19.6m of $29.5m in FY2025) is the swing line and looks soft. It was $4.8m in Q1 and $4.8m in Q2 2026 (Q2 -4% YoY, 'SaaS performance weaker than expected', 'renewal pricing pressure', insufficient new bookings), against a Q3 2025 comp of $5.1m, so a flat sequential print is ~-6% YoY. The Oct-15 KPI release also changed its wording: from July's 'Solutions progress will be discussed in the upcoming earnings release' to 'Solutions, which account for the majority of Freightos' revenue, are less directly reflected in these metrics. The Company will provide an update on Solutions performance'. That reads as a hedge. Net of Platform at ~$3.0-3.1m, total revenue reaches the $7.83-7.90m consensus only if Solutions is >= ~$4.8m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: revenue lagged estimates while KPIs beat, stock -13.9%. Q4 2025 (2026-02-23): -30%, conflated with the founder's board exit (https://www.freightwaves.com/news/freightos-stock-plummets-after-founder-resigns). Q2 2026: Solutions -4% was offset by a Platform/Clearit beat, +14%.

findings.finding: The freight-rate backdrop since the guide was set is stronger, which supports a Q4/FY GBV raise. The guide 'assumes freight price levels and market volumes as of August 2026'. WorldACD global air rates were $3.45/kg in week 45 (2-8 Nov 2026), +31% YoY; late-October spot was reported +38% YoY. Tonnage was flat to down. Platform revenue tracks transactions more than rates (Q3 2025: GBV +54%, Platform +15%), so the transmission to revenue is weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent. The Q2 2026 call kept FY GBV +19-21% after a Q2 GBV beat, and the stock rose +14% on the revenue/EBITDA beat, not on GBV.

findings.finding: Q4 2026 is the guided EBITDA-breakeven quarter. Guide: Q4 adj. EBITDA loss under $1m, crossing breakeven 'at some point during Q4', with the full impact of the March cost actions landing in Q4. Q2 liquidity was $21.4m (cash $13.3m plus $8.1m deposit) with burn tracking adj. EBITDA, and management said no financing is needed. Q3-end liquidity should therefore be ~$20m against a ~$41.7m market cap. A reaffirmation on the call lands on the guide and the cash path. The money question (lesson 4) was answered: no raise is planned, so it is not a negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: 'lowest-ever adj. EBITDA loss' plus reiterated breakeven, +14% pre-market. FY2025 print (Feb 2026): breakeven reiterated, but the stock fell -30% on the founder's exit.
